args: In libredwg/src/bits.c, what boundary-check style should bit_read_BB use to ensure two bits are available, and are there existing helpers/tests that cover reads at the exact end or at bit 7 of the last byte? Please focus on a minimal root-cause fix in C source.

The sanitizer report shows bit_read_BB at libredwg/src/bits.c:198 dereferencing dat->chain[dat->byte] when dat->byte == dat->size and dat->bit == 0. The current CHK_OVERFLOW macro accepts the exact end because it checks only a cursor beyond the end, and bit_read_BB requests two bits. At bit 7 of the final byte it also lacks the second requested bit; current code returns only the first bit and advances beyond the end. I am considering a local overflow-safe availability check before dereference, expressed without multiplying sizes or adding to potentially large cursor values.
